advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In _open_slot, distinguish contention (EWOULDBLOCK/EAGAIN → None) from a locking-unsupported OSError (ENOLCK/EOPNOTSUPP → propagate so the caller can DISARM), rather than swallowing all OSError as 'slot taken'.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py:144-148: `try:` / `fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)` / `except OSError:` / `os.close(fd); return None`
Docstring at :136 asserts `None` means "another holder has it" — but ENOLCK/EOPNOTSUPP also raise OSError here and are indistinguishable from EWOULDBLOCK/EAGAIN

gate_admission()'s design (module docstring, :226-229) DISARMS (admit + GATE_ADMISSION_DISARMED) when `fcntl is None`, i.e. treats a platform locking gap as fail-open; a filesystem that raises ENOLCK reaches the opposite (permanent refusal) path
advisory.finding: _open_slot() collapses EVERY OSError from fcntl.flock into a None ('slot already held') result, but flock also raises OSError for non-contention reasons — most importantly ENOLCK / EOPNOTSUPP on a filesystem without working advisory locking (e.g. NFS without lockd). In that case acquire_slot() sees all slots as taken and gate_admission() raises GateCongestedError for every run, permanently and falsely, instead of DISARMING (fail-open) the way the fcntl-absent branch does. A locking-unsupported store is a platform gap, not host congestion.
scenarios: Snapshot store (REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR) on an NFS mount without lockd, or any FS returning ENOLCK/EOPNOTSUPP for flock
advisory.suggested_fix: In the except block, re-raise (or signal disarm) when errno not in (EAGAIN, EWOULDBLOCK); only return None for genuine lock contention.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a CLI test that raises GateCongestedError (and GateScratchUnavailableError) from verify_completion and asserts the verify-completion CLI handler returns exit 11.
evidence: Diff comment src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:379-380: 'Its own arm because this handler — unlike verify-completion's — hardcodes 1 for an LLMError.'
Only review_plan CLI arm is tested: `code = _llm_commands._review_plan(["09da-343c-1ee9-480c"]); assert code == 11`
ABSENCE: no test invokes the verify-completion CLI handler with a raised GateCongestedError/GateScratchUnavailableError to confirm exit 11 through the shared _llm_error_exit_code path.
src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:376 `except _admission_refusal() as exc:` where `_admission_refusal()` returns `(GateCongestedError, GateScratchUnavailableError)`
src/rebar/llm/errors.py: GateScratchUnavailableError sets `self.outcome = _admission_outcome("gate_scratch_unavailable", gate)` with retryable=True
ABSENCE: the only CLI exit-code test raises GateCongestedError; no test raises GateScratchUnavailableError through _review_plan to assert exit 11.
advisory.finding: The verify-completion CLI handler's routing of gate-admission refusals to exit 11 is asserted by the diff narrative ('a retryable ... exit 11 on the CLI ... rather than each call site growing a clause') but is never tested: no test drives GateCongestedError or GateScratchUnavailableError through verify-completion's CLI handler. Only review_plan's new narrow arm is CLI-tested (test_the_cli_reports_congestion_as_a_transient_retry_exit_code). A regression that made verify-completion's pre-existing LLMError arm return a non-11 code for an admission refusal would not be caught.
merged_from: GateScratchUnavailableError at the CLI (exit 11) is untested. The newly added CLI arm `except _admission_refusal()` catches BOTH GateCongestedError and GateScratchUnavailableError, and GateScratchUnavailableError carries a retryable outcome intended to produce exit 11, but only its MCP surface is tested (test_the_scratch_refusal_is_retryable_over_mcp). The named violating input — GateScratchUnavailableError raised at the review-plan CLI — has no test asserting exit 11.
scenarios: A future refactor of verify-completion's CLI except arms silently downgrades an admission refusal to exit 1, mis-signalling a transient host condition as a hard failure to the review bot.
advisory.suggested_fix: Mirror test_the_cli_reports_congestion_as_a_transient_retry_exit_code against the verify-completion CLI entry point, asserting the returned code is 11 for both admission-refusal error types.
